full_judgment:
8. He further submits that the amendment application is barred by limitation and nature and character completely changed by the proposed amendment. In support of his contention he referred the case of (3) Hosne Zaman Sacker -vs- Election Tribunal and Munsif and others, reported in 38 DLR 435. (4) Zulfiquar Ali Bhutto-vs- Bangladesh and others, reported in 41 DLR-379. 

 "In that view of the matter the power an Election Tribunal deciding an election petition under section 27 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance 1983, is that of statutory tribunal with limited jurisdiction. The provision of rule 47 of the said Rules that the Code of Civil Procedure shall, as nearly as possible, be followed in trying election cases, does not mean that the Tribunal has the power of making an amendment of the election petition so as to make it relate back to the date of filing of the said petition. In other words, even though the Tribunal is not a Civil Court exercising all the powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, it may still exercise the power of amendment of pleadings, but it has no authority to give the amendment a retrospective effect from the date of filing of the election petition." (4) 41 DLR 379, wherein it has been held: "Thus although the Election Tribunal has the limited jurisdiction to allow amendment of the election petition, it has no power to allow any amendment, so as to relate back to the date of filing of the election petition. It is so because sub-rule(1) of Rule 44 prescribed the limitation of 30 days next after the publication of the result in the official Gazette to file an election petition and sub-rule(5) specifically provides that an election petition shall set forth the ground on which the petition is fixed and the relief sought. In other words the ground for the election petition and the relief sought must be stated within the period of limitation."
